name: Scale AI
monetization: Sells training data — labeling, RLHF, and expert data pipelines — plus government AI services; now effectively a Meta-aligned data arm after the 2025 quasi-acquisition.
description_md: Scale AI built the dominant data-labeling and human-feedback pipeline of the first LLM wave, supplying OpenAI, Google, Meta, xAI, and the Pentagon. In June 2025 Meta paid $14.3B for a 49% non-voting stake (implying ~$29B) and hired away founder-CEO Alexandr Wang to run Meta Superintelligence Labs — a 'quasi-M&A' that instantly cost Scale its neutrality and triggered an exodus of its largest lab customers. The valuation has been frozen at the Meta mark since.
ai_monetization_md: Pre-deal, revenue (~$870M in 2024, roughly doubling y/y) came from frontier labs paying for labeled/preference data — Google alone was worth ~$150–200M/yr — plus a growing public-sector business (Scale Donovan; defense contracts). Post-deal, Google, OpenAI, xAI, and Microsoft all cut or wound down work, leaving Meta itself, enterprises, and government as the remaining pillars. The rise of expert-generated data rivals (Surge, Mercor, Turing — Surge out-earned Scale in 2024 at $1B+ bootstrapped) was already compressing the core labeling franchise.
ai_strategy_md: The Meta transaction converted Scale from neutral infrastructure into aligned capacity: Meta secured data pipelines and Wang's team without a reviewable acquisition (49%, non-voting), while Scale shareholders got liquidity at ~$29B. Remaining strategy under CEO Jason Droege leans on government/defense AI (where neutrality vs Meta matters less) and enterprise data engines, while the frontier-lab market it created moves to competitors positioned as conflict-free.
risk_notes_md: Customer-concentration inversion: the deal that crystallized its valuation destroyed its customer base — Google (largest customer) split, OpenAI dropped Scale as a data provider, xAI and Microsoft backed away, and Scale laid off ~14% of staff (~200 roles) in July 2025. The $14.3B is Meta's cost basis, not evidence of Scale's standalone earning power; no post-deal revenue figures are public (informative in itself). Antitrust/structure scrutiny of 49% non-voting 'acqui-stakes' remains a live regulatory theme.

events.title: Meta invests $14.3B for 49% non-voting stake; Wang leaves to lead Meta Superintelligence Labs
events.why_it_matters: The template 'quasi-M&A' of the cycle: control-like economics without a reviewable acquisition. Values Scale at ~$29B and staffs Meta's superintelligence push, but ends Scale's position as neutral data infrastructure.

events.title: Customer exodus: OpenAI drops Scale; Google, xAI, Microsoft pull back
events.why_it_matters: Within days of the Meta deal, Scale's largest lab customers cut ties over data-security and roadmap-leak concerns — a clean case study of how ownership changes destroy 'neutral vendor' revenue. Scale cut ~14% of staff the following month.
